brief: Replace text or regular expression matches
description: Replace matches in a anyURI value, left to right, up to limit times, as ECMAScript's s.replace(search, r) does. search is a string, which is literal text, or a regexp, which is a pattern. An empty match is a match at a code-point boundary. The default limit replaces once (an empty string inserts at the start). Specify limit -1 to replace every match.

parameters.description: What to replace: a string is literal text, and an empty string matches at each code-point boundary, including the start and the end; a regexp is a pattern. A regexp literal (/a+b/ or "a+b"re), to_regexp(s), or compile<regexp>(r) is already compiled; any other regexp value is compiled for this call.
parameters.name: search

parameters.description: The replacement for each match. When search is a string, the replacement is literal text. When search is a regexp, $n is the text of group n ($0 the whole match), ${name} the text of a named group, and a backslash makes the next character literal (\$ for a dollar sign); any other $ is an error.
parameters.name: replacement

parameters.description: The maximum number of matches to replace. The default is 1. Specify -1 (or any negative) to replace every match.
parameters.name: limit

returns.description: Result text as string (not re-typed as the input data type).
